transcript:
Header: Redwood internal launch safety sync
Date: 2026-06-04 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Priya, Diego, Sofia, Liam, Alicia, Tom, Rachel, Marcus

Summary: quick postmortem from the beta canary (weekend flux), identify short-term mitigations and long-term fixes; align on canary ramp schedule, fallback routing, KMS rotation and audit artifacts.

---
00:00 Priya: okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, I know we have a packed agenda. quick show of hands, did folks get last night's incident notes?
00:08 Alicia: yes, I skimmed through, looks like two areas —cache warm-up and a routing mis-match during the failover.
00:14 Diego: mhm, and the quantized variant slipped past perf guardrails at high concurrency so latency tail spiked, so that was the main signal.
00:22 Tom: i can say from release side the autoscale didn't pick up the extra evic—eviction churn fast enough. there's a timing window.
00:29 Rachel: and we saw elevated error rates downstream in the scorer service, which amplified the retries and created a feedback loop.
00:36 Priya: okay, let's step through timeline then actions. Diego, quick TL;DR on KV cache behavior and the quant experiment that triggered it?
00:44 Diego: yeah. we deployed quant-profile-c on Saturday night as part of the canary. workload si — workload sim was okay under 70% utilization, but under the real traffic mixing we had prefix misses. The KV cache warmed slower because of the mixed-session distribution; that caused more full-token generation calls which leaned on a slower kernel path for the quantized model. so tail latency jumped.
01:05 Alicia: sorry, when you say "slower kernel path" you mean the CPU fallback or the different attention kernel?
01:09 Diego: mostly attention kernel fallback — the quantized operator fell back to a non-optimized path for long sequence lengths; also we saw some CPU fallback for KV eviction while the gpu was under memory pressure.
01:18 Marcus: memory pressure — any indication we hit HBM OOMs? I didn't see OOM logs but there's elevated allocator retries.
01:24 Diego: no hard OOM, but memory trimming events yes. the allocator retried and that lengthened the critical path.
01:30 Sofia: this aligns with the autoscaler window Tom mentioned — the nodes didn't add capacity fast enough to absorb the transient.
01:36 Tom: right. our scale-up policy has a 45s stabilization which is too slow for a spike that came in 20s.
01:42 Priya: ok two buckets: short-term mitigations (canary rollback, temp throttle, adjust scale window) and medium-term fixes (kernel fallback telemetry, new perf gates for quant profiles).
01:51 Liam: from CSM/ops perspective we also need a clear comms plan if we pause canary or rollback, when to notify customers. Alicia, you're on that?
01:58 Alicia: yep i'll draft messaging. want to avoid over-notifying but be transparent.
02:03 Marcus: security note — any rollback or config changes touching KMS keys must pass change control; we need to log key access and rotation steps. if we plan key reuse for test canaries that needs scrutiny.
02:12 Priya: good point. Sofia, can you walk through the proposed canary ramp with fallback windows?
02:17 Sofia: sure. proposal: day 0 small traffic 0.5% for 1 hour, day 1 2% for 3 hours, day 2 10% with autoscale enabled and a hard fallback to hosted variant on error threshold. fallback policy: if p95 latency > 750ms or errors > 1% for 2 consecutive 5m windows, route to hosted S1 model in same region, then pause ramp.
02:40 Diego: add a KV-cache priming job during pre-ramp so prefix misses drop — we can replay a 24h session sample to warm the caches.
02:48 Tom: question — that priming will add load; we'd want to run it on reserved capacity so it doesn't affect live traffic.
02:53 Sofia: agreed, run during maintenance window on dedicated pool.
02:57 Priya: action: Diego to prepare priming script; Sofia to schedule maintenance reservation.
03:03 Rachel: on observability, we need better kernel-level metrics surfaced in console — per-operator latency and fallback counts. current traces don't show why a token got CPU-fallback.
03:12 Diego: tracing span exists but we don't emit operator ID to the trace consistently — i'll file a small change to include it.
03:17 Priya: add to actions.
03:21 Alicia: quick question — do we keep quant-profile-c in the model catalog marked as "experimental" or pull it until we fix perf gates?
03:29 Diego: i'd mark it experimental and pin canary to quant-profile-b for now. quant-c requires better perf gating.
03:34 Marcus: security/reg compliance — also want to ensure audit logs capture the canary-to-hosted fallback events and any key usage. SOC2 auditors will ask.
03:42 Priya: Liam, can you coordinate with Marcus on the audit artifact list?
03:46 Liam: yes. i'll add that as an item and include a timeline.
03:49 Tom: another root cause angle — routing mis-match: during failover some requests were routed to an older variant because our route table took longer to sync cross-region, leading to model-variant incompatibility and extra model loads.
04:05 Sofia: that's a control-plane propagation issue. we should either version-check requests or ensure concurrent variant compatibility.
04:11 Diego: simple mitigation: add a model-variant compatibility shim that rejects or redirects incompatible requests rather than loading the wrong weights.
04:18 Priya: good. let's add that to medium-term backlog.
04:22 Alicia: customers will ask about data retention during canary — are logs persisted, PII redaction?
04:28 Marcus: logs are stored 90 days by default, sensitive fields masked; but we need to document retention and show where redaction happens in pipeline. i'll prep a short diagram.
04:36 Priya: excellent. now, decisions we need today: 1) rollback quant-profile-c from canary and mark experimental, 2) run KV priming on reserved pool before next ramp, 3) shorten autoscale stabilization for canary nodes to 15s, 4) enable fallback routing to hosted S1 with threshold. any objections?
04:56 Tom: objection on 3 — changing stabilization globally is risky. make it a scoped override for canary only.
05:01 Priya: yes scoped override only. agreed.
05:04 Sofia: we need clear guardrails to revert the override automatically after canary ends.
05:09 Diego: and we need to run the quant regression suite across seq lengths up to 8k to be sure.
05:14 Priya: noted.
05:16 Liam: on comms, proposed cadence: immediate short note to pilot customers (if we're pausing), a follow-up postmortem shared 24h after full postmortem is compiled, and a scheduled review with key accounts next week.
05:28 Alicia: i'll prepare the pilot note and the stakeholder list.
05:31 Priya: ok let's allocate owners and due dates. (we list them in the action items).
05:36 Rachel: ops readiness — i'd like a dry-run of the fallback plan tomorrow in staging: simulate the error threshold and ensure route switch completes without leftover sessions.
05:44 Sofia: we can script that and run in staging at 02:00 UTC — i'll coordinate.
05:48 Diego: also include a load test to simulate the priming job effect and monitor eviction rates.
05:53 Priya: good. anything else on incident root causes?
05:56 Tom: one more small note — our artifact for model packaging didn't include a checksum field; that contributed to a subtle deploy race. we should include a packaging checksum in the image metadata.
06:05 Diego: agreed. tiny change but helps guardrails.
06:08 Priya: okay, let's do a quick readout for execs at 17:00 today — 5 minute slide: current status, mitigations, ask (approval for scoped autoscale override, reservation for priming).
06:18 Liam: i'll take the exec slide and run it by Priya at 16:30.
06:22 Priya: excellent. final check — any blockers on the security sign-off for priming or fallback?
06:27 Marcus: i'll need the exact KMS access pattern for the priming job; if it uses test keys that's fine, if it touches production keys we need change control.
06:34 Sofia: priming will use a dedicated test key in HSM, not prod. i'll document.
06:38 Priya: wrap up: Diego, Sofia, Marcus, Alicia — owners on the top items. we reconvene 2026-06-07 14:00 UTC for canary ramp review.
06:47 Alicia: noted.
06:49 Diego: noted.
06:50 Priya: cool thanks everyone. end.

Notes: transcript has occasional filler and mis-attributions from automated captioning; operator IDs and precise kernel names to be filled in code review.
